To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nuclear matrix elements are the main source of uncertainties in the calculation of neutrinoless beta decay half-lifes and that, in the context of seesaw models, large rates of neutrinos double beta decay are compatible with cosmological bounds on the masses of the extra neutrinos.

(i) the uncertainties in the nuclear matrix elements are of the order of a factor 3, and that they are dominated by the truncation of the Hilbert space; (ii) in the type I seesaws, the contribution of the heavy Majorana neutrinos to the nuclear matrix elements is negligible, unless they have masses in the range of 10^7 GeV, which is excluded by cosmological observations;
the nuclear matrix elements of neutrinoless ββ decay are uncertain by a factor of about 2-3.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the uncertainty associated to the different nuclear matrix elements? What is the dependence of these matrix elements on the exchange neutrino mass? What are the contributions to the neutrino exchange mechanism of the extra neutrinos of seesaw models? In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the uncertainties associated with the nuclear matrix elements are the main source of error in the determination of the half-life of neutrinoless beta beta decay.

the neutrinoless beta decay is a powerful tool in the quest for the neutrino nature, and that a large effort is still required to reach the ultimate goal of a precise determination of the neutrino masses and the Majorana nature of the neutrino.

the uncertainties in the calculation of nuclear matrix elements are of the same order of magnitude as the uncertainties in the neutrino mass parameters, so that a conclusive statement on the neutrino mass scale is not yet possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the nuclear physics uncertainties associated to the shell model calculation of the nuclear structure matrix elements are not the dominant source of uncertainties in the neutrinoless beta beta decay rate.
the neutrinoless decay rate is very sensitive to the nuclear matrix elements and to the neutrino mass spectrum, but it is not very sensitive to the neutrino exchange mechanism.
the nuclear matrix elements of the neutrinoless beta decay are very sensitive to the mass of the neutrino, but not very sensitive to the details of the nuclear wavefunctions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in order to extract reliable information about the neutrinos masses from the experimental data, it is necessary to improve the precision of the nuclear matrix element calculations, in particular, by including the effect of the nuclear deformation.
the neutrinoless decay is dominated by the lightest neutrino mass eigenstate.
the neutrinoless decay rate is not only a function of the neutrino mass but also a function of the nuclear matrix element, which is not yet well known.
